card.name: dyadic_rz_phase_gradient_catalysis
card.precondition: family dv_angle; needs nonclifford_rz and ancilla_room; min_qubits 2, max_qubits 20. Fires only if at least 8 non-Clifford rz angles are exact multiples of pi/2^m for some m <= 8 (|theta - k*pi/2^m| <= 1e-12 via v4.api.angles.dyadic). qft_8 satisfies this maximally: fingerprint exactly_dyadic[8] = 33 of 33 off-grid rotations.
card.identity: Prepare ONE catalyst register of M = 9 qubits in the phase-gradient state |g> = 2^(-M/2) sum_y e^(-2*pi*i*y/2^M)|y>, i.e. one Rz(-2*pi/2^j) (= one rotation of angle 2*pi/2^j) on each gradient bit j = 1..M after Hadamards; j = 1,2,3 are Clifford/T, only j = 4..9 need gridsynth, and they are paid ONCE for the whole circuit. Then replace every rotation rz(theta) with theta = k*pi/2^m (m <= 8, k odd) on qubit q by: a q-controlled addition of the CLASSICAL constant c = k * 2^(M-m-1) into the gradient register mod 2^M, built from m and_compute gadgets (4 T each) on one clean carry ancilla, m cx/x fix-ups, and m measurement-based and_uncompute (0 T). The gradient register comes out in |g> again (catalysis: it is restored, not consumed, so all 33 rotations share one preparation), the carry ancilla returns to |0>, and no rotation on the data qubits remains for gridsynth to synthesize. This is NOT in the floor tier of this book (BOOK.md floor = dpf_dyadic_angle_fixing + the two pyzx-class Pauli merges only); it differs from a register-register adder construction in that each rotation becomes a CONSTANT addition, whose trailing M-m-1 zero bits are free, so the cost is 4m T and not 4M T.
card.correctness: Adding c mod 2^M to |g> gives 2^(-M/2) sum_y e^(-2*pi*i*y/2^M)|y+c> = e^(+2*pi*i*c/2^M) |g> by reindexing z = y+c (the sum is cyclic, so mod-2^M addition is exactly the shift that reproduces the state). The adder is therefore a unitary that multiplies by the scalar e^(2*pi*i*c/2^M) and leaves the register invariant. Controlling it on q puts that scalar only on the |1>_q branch, i.e. diag(1, e^(2*pi*i*c/2^M)) on q = Rz(2*pi*c/2^(M-1)) up to global phase; with c = k*2^(M-m-1) this is exactly Rz(k*pi/2^m) = the deleted gate. Since the gate is diagonal in the computational basis of q, the substitution is valid at any position in the op list, Hadamards included. The and_compute/and_uncompute gadgets are Gidney's temporary AND: exact, and the uncompute is an X-basis measurement with a classically controlled CZ fix-up, so the ancilla is deterministically returned to |0> on every branch and the Kraus operator of every measurement branch is the same unitary up to the same phase (invariant 2 holds branch-wise). The only error is the finite-precision synthesis of the 6 gradient-preparation rotations; the whole-circuit judge measures the phase-aligned distance of the result against the ORIGINAL circuit, which is what the drawn budget covers.
card.trigger: Scan the op list for ops with rotation(op) not None and not on_grid(theta); for each, let d = angles.nearest(theta, kmax=8) and keep the match if d.distance == 0 (exact dyadic) and 3 <= d.m <= 8. Emit one match per such rotation, plus a single circuit-level match that appends the M = 9 gradient qubits and 1 carry ancilla (append_ancillas) and emits the preparation prefix / its inverse suffix. If fewer than 8 rotation matches survive, emit nothing (the one-time preparation cost cannot be amortized).
card.expected_effect: All 33 off-grid rz on the 8 data qubits disappear, so gridsynth pays for 0 of them instead of 33 at eps_rz = 3.03e-5 (~45 T each, which is essentially the whole current 1583). They are replaced by 4m T of exact AND gadgets each: by the fingerprint's level histogram (8 rotations at m=3, 7 at m=4, 6 at m=5, 5 at m=6, 4 at m=7, 3 at m=8) that is 8*12 + 7*16 + 6*20 + 5*24 + 4*28 + 3*32 = 656 T, plus ~270 T for the 6 off-grid gradient-preparation rotations synthesized once at eps ~2.5e-5 (0.00015 drawn, split 6 ways), plus the 11 explicit t/tdg that stay. Expected total ~930 T on 18 qubits (8 data + 9 gradient + 1 carry), i.e. below DPF Synth's 1064 on 34 qubits. Scored conservatively against the current 1583 in case the carry ancilla needs a second qubit and the preparation is charged at full eps_rz.
card.source: Kitaev, Shen & Vyalyi, Classical and Quantum Computation (2002), phase kickback / phase-gradient eigenstate; C. Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition', Quantum 2, 74 (2018) (temporary-AND gadget, 4 T compute + 0 T measured uncompute) and 'Turning gradients into additions into QFTs' (2016); Gidney & Ekera, Quantum 5, 433 (2021), Appendix C (phase-gradient catalyst reused across all rotations).

summary: The rule fires and verifies, but lowers no circuit's T-count beyond the current book. The idea does not pay here. Propose a different idea.

card.name: hamming_weight_phasing_equal_angle_groups_2
card.precondition: family dv_angle; needs nonclifford_rz and ancilla_room; min_qubits 2, max_qubits 20. Fires only if, after v4.api.pauli.frames, the off-grid rotations contain at least one equal-|angle| class of multiplicity k >= 3 whose members pairwise commute (sign absorbed into the Pauli: Rz(-t) about P = Rz(t) about -P). qft_8 satisfies this maximally: the angle histogram is the QFT ladder pi/2^m with multiplicities 6 (pi/8), 5 (pi/16), 4 (pi/32), 3 (pi/64), 2 (pi/128) out of 33 off-grid rotations. NOTE on levers: the fingerprint's rotation_count headroom of 2 counts only pyzx-class EQUAL-AXIS unitary merges, which the floor already took. This rule removes rotations that have DIFFERENT axes but the SAME angle, which is unreachable unitarily and is bought with clean ancillas + measurement - the same lever by which DPF Synth reaches 1064 on 34 qubits, here used exactly and on <= 17 qubits.
card.identity: For k commuting rotations of the SAME angle theta about Paulis P_1..P_k, prod_i exp(-i theta P_i / 2) depends only on the number of P_i that evaluate to -1. Realize each P_i as Z on a distinct wire (parity copy by a CNOT ladder onto one clean ancilla per member, local Cliffords first if P_i is X/Y-type), giving prod_i Rz(theta)_{a_i} = exp(-i (theta/2) sum_i Z_{a_i}). Since sum_i Z_{a_i} = k - 2*HW(x), compute the Hamming weight HW(x) = sum_j 2^j w_j of the k ancillas into b = floor(log2 k)+1 weight bits with a tree of full adders (one and_compute each, 4 T, plus CNOT/X fix-ups), then apply ONE rotation Rz(2^j * theta) on each weight bit w_j, then uncompute the adder tree with and_uncompute (0 T, X-basis measurement + classically controlled CZ) and undo the parity copies. k rotations of angle theta become b rotations of angles theta, 2theta, ..., 2^(b-1) theta, and every one with 2^j|theta| >= pi/4 is Clifford/T, so gridsynth pays for it nothing. This is Hamming weight phasing; it is NOT phase folding (axes differ), NOT angle snapping (no angle is moved), and NOT a phase-gradient/constant-addition construction (no gradient catalyst register, no shared resource state, nothing amortized across the circuit - each angle class pays its own small adder tree and the rule is exact).
card.correctness: Each P_i is Hermitian with eigenvalues +-1 and the P_i pairwise commute, so they are simultaneously diagonalizable and the k exponentials may be slid to one common slice provided each P_i also commutes with every rotation Pauli strictly between the earliest and latest member (checked by the trigger) - Clifford ops between them are absorbed by the frame sweep, which is exact up to global phase. Parity copy: CNOTs from the support of P_i onto a clean ancilla a_i put x_i = P_i's eigenvalue bit on a_i, with the data unchanged; conjugating by it maps Z_{a_i} to P_i exactly, and the ladder is its own inverse. On the copies, prod_i exp(-i theta Z_{a_i}/2) = exp(-i(theta/2)(k - 2 HW(x))) = e^{-i theta k/2} * exp(i theta HW(x)); the global scalar is unobservable. With HW(x) = sum_j 2^j w_j, exp(i theta HW) = prod_j exp(i theta 2^j w_j) = prod_j Rz(-2^j theta) on w_j up to another global phase, because w_j is a computational-basis bit and the operator is diagonal. The full-adder tree computing HW is a reversible classical circuit, and Gidney's temporary-AND gadget is exact: its uncompute measures the target in the X basis and applies a classically controlled CZ, so on EVERY measurement branch the Kraus operator is the same unitary times the same scalar and the ancilla is returned to |0> deterministically (invariant 2 holds branch-wise, which is exactly what the judge's branch-wise specification check tests). Total error introduced: zero; the only error in the final circuit remains gridsynth's on the surviving rotations, which is cheaper than before because there are fewer of them.
card.trigger: Run pauli.frames(ops) to get Records (pos, theta, Pauli, on_grid). Drop records with on_grid. Normalize: replace (theta<0, P) by (|theta|, -P). Bucket by |theta| to 1e-9. For each bucket of size k >= 3, greedily take a maximal subset S that is pairwise commuting (pauli.commutes) and such that every member's Pauli commutes with the Pauli of every rotation record whose pos lies between min(pos in S) and max(pos in S). Let b = floor(log2 |S|) + 1 and let g = #{ j in [0,b) : 2^j * |theta| is a multiple of pi/4 (on_grid) }. Emit the match only if |S| - (b - g) >= 1, i.e. the number of off-grid rotations strictly falls; the match carries S, the common slice position (the position of the last member), the b weight bits and the |S| parity ancillas requested via append_ancillas. Emit one match per bucket, largest |S| first. On qft_8 this emits 4 matches: |S|=6 at pi/8 (b=3, weight angles pi/8, pi/4, pi/2 -> 1 off-grid, saves 5), |S|=5 at pi/16 (b=3 -> pi/16, pi/8, pi/4 -> 2 off-grid, saves 3), |S|=4 at pi/32 (b=3 -> 3 off-grid, saves 1), |S|=3 at pi/64 (b=2 -> 2 off-grid, saves 1); the pi/128 pair is correctly skipped by the net-reduction test.
card.expected_effect: The off-grid rotation count falls 33 -> 23 (-10), each worth ~47.6 T at eps_rz = 3.03e-5 (1572 T buys the current 33). Added cost is exact and small: the adder trees for the four groups need (6-3)+(5-3)+(4-3)+(3-2) = 7 full adders = 7 and_compute = 28 T, their uncompute is 0 T, and the parity copies plus fix-ups are pure Clifford (CNOT count rises, which is only the third cost key). Surviving on-grid weight-bit rotations (pi/4, pi/2 and the T-level pi/8 at j=0 of no group) are free or cheap. Resources: <= 18 parity+weight ancillas requested but reusable per group, so <= 6+3 live at once -> 17 qubits, half of DPF Synth's 34. Estimated 1583 -> ~1180, scored conservatively in case one group's commutation guard fails and only three of the four matches survive.
card.source: I. D. Kivlichan, C. Gidney, D. W. Berry, N. Wiebe, J. McClean, W. Sun, Z. Jiang, N. Rubin, A. Fowler, A. Aspuru-Guzik, H. Neven, R. Babbush, 'Improved Fault-Tolerant Quantum Simulation of Condensed-Phase Correlated Electrons via Trotterization', Quantum 4, 296 (2020), Sec. 'Hamming weight phasing'; temporary-AND gadget from C. Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition', Quantum 2, 74 (2018).

summary: lever 'ancilla_reconstruction' has no headroom left on qft_8 (consumed by relaxed rules only)
